title: Theo and the Letters
premise: Coral Whitlock, a cellist whose career shattered in one catastrophic final performance, has spent ten years exchanging anonymous letters with someone who signed only 'T' — the only relationship that never asked her to perform. When Theo, her letter-writer, moves in next door without revealing their identity, Coral begins falling for them in person while feeling guilty of betraying the pen pal she believes is her truest self. As Theo's quiet campaign of justice against the conductor who destroyed Coral's career escalates into something dangerous, Coral discovers the truth: Theo orchestrated both her ruin and her rescue years ago, and now stands to lose everything protecting her from the fallout. In the end, Coral must choose between reclaiming the stage on the conductor's terms and testifying beside Theo — and she chooses the person who saw her clearly first, playing one final, unscripted concert as the law closes in.
about_author: Coral Coldharbour is the pen name of a former orchestral librarian who spent fifteen years backstage at concert halls before turning to fiction. They write romances about people whose private selves are larger than their public performances.

chapters.title: The Broken String
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, ten years after her disastrous final performance. A flashback interwoven with her present as a music teacher who no longer performs. She rereads the latest letter from 'T,' her anonymous correspondent of a decade. Emotional beat: grief calcified into routine, and the small warmth the letters still provide.

chapters.title: Moving Vans on Marlowe Street
chapters.summary: Coral watches a new neighbor unload boxes — among them, a crate of sheet music she recognizes. First meeting is awkward; the neighbor, Theo, is guarded but kind, helping when her cat escapes. POV Coral. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity, an inexplicable sense of familiarity she dismisses.

chapters.title: What T Never Wrote
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, revealing they are indeed the letter-writer but chose not to say so — guilt over an old secret keeping them silent. We learn Theo works as an investigator for a legal-aid nonprofit. Emotional beat: longing restrained by fear of what honesty would cost.

chapters.title: Duet in a Doorway
chapters.summary: A shared umbrella, a borrowed cello stand, a first real conversation about music. Coral plays for Theo through the wall, not knowing why that feels safe. POV alternating. Emotional beat: the first spark — two people circling something neither names.

chapters.title: Letters, Numbered
chapters.summary: Coral organizes her decade of letters chronologically and notices patterns: T always knew things about the classical world T shouldn't know. Meanwhile Theo writes letter #113 by hand, hesitating over a confession. POV both. Emotional beat: suspicion blooming alongside affection.

chapters.title: The Conductor's Name
chapters.summary: Coral learns Maestro Aldous Vane — the man who publicly blamed her for the catastrophic premiere — is being investigated for financial fraud and artistic blacklisting. Theo's nonprofit is involved. Coral realizes the case could restore her reputation. POV Coral. Emotional beat: hope, sharp and frightening.

chapters.title: Coffee, Almost
chapters.summary: Theo and Coral's almost-date is interrupted by a call from Theo's casework. Coral glimpses a file on Vane in Theo's bag and feels the pieces shift. POV Theo. Emotional beat: the cost of divided loyalty; Theo lies for the first time and hates it.

chapters.title: Letter #114
chapters.summary: Coral receives a letter that describes her new neighbor too precisely. She confronts the possibility that T lives nearby — maybe next door. She tests Theo with a fabricated detail from the letters. POV Coral. Emotional beat: vertigo between betrayal and hope.

chapters.title: The Test
chapters.summary: Theo passes Coral's fabricated-detail trap because Theo wrote it — but realizes mid-conversation they've been caught lying about something else. A charged argument about trust, neither naming the real secret. POV Theo. Emotional beat: intimacy deepening even as deception compounds.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Maestro Vane approaches Coral directly: he'll publicly exonerate her and offer a comeback tour if she publicly discredits the investigation. The career she mourned, dangled like bait. POV Coral. Emotional beat: temptation wearing the mask of justice.

chapters.title: What the Letters Were For
chapters.summary: Revelation: Theo began writing to Coral ten years ago out of guilt — Theo was the young assistant who smuggled Vane the doctored review that ended her career. The letters were penance. POV Theo, full flashback. Emotional beat: shame transformed into devotion, and the terror of confession.

chapters.title: Midnight Practice
chapters.summary: Coral, unable to sleep, plays cello at 2 a.m. Theo comes to the door, and they finally kiss — then Coral finds letter drafts in Theo's coat pocket. She says nothing. POV Coral. Emotional beat: joy poisoned by evidence, love chosen anyway.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower
chapters.summary: A witness in the Vane case recants after threats. Theo's investigation teeters. Coral realizes Vane's people are watching her apartment — watching Theo. POV Theo. Emotional beat: danger arriving at the doorstep; protectiveness hardening into recklessness.

chapters.title: Broken Glass
chapters.summary: Someone breaks into Coral's home and destroys her cello — a message from Vane. Theo arrives too late, holds her amid the wreckage, and nearly confesses everything. POV Coral. Emotional beat: violation and fury; the old catastrophe echoing in the new one.

chapters.title: Confession, Letter #115
chapters.summary: Theo leaves the truth on Coral's doorstep in a sealed letter and prepares to testify alone, expecting to lose her. Coral reads it at dawn: the sabotage, the guilt, the decade of letters as atonement. POV alternating. Emotional beat: devastation — and recognition that the letters were always honest about everything except their origin.

chapters.title: Silence Between Walls
chapters.summary: Days of silence. Coral teaches, doesn't write back, can't stop reading letter #115. Her students' recital forces her to confront what music means when stripped of career. POV Coral. Emotional beat: the slow turn from betrayal toward understanding.

chapters.title: Vane's Gambit
chapters.summary: Vane threatens to expose Theo's role in the original sabotage, framing Theo as a blackmailer. He offers Coral a final deal: her career restored if she denounces Theo publicly. POV Vane-adjacent via Coral's confrontation with him. Emotional beat: power showing its rotten core; Coral sees the trap whole.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Coral walks into the hearing room uninvited and takes the stand beside Theo, surrendering any chance of Vane's protection. She tells the truth about the sabotage — including Theo's part. POV Coral. Emotional beat: climax; identity reclaimed not through the stage but through testimony.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: The ruling lands: Vane is indicted; Theo faces consequences for the decade-old act but receives leniency for cooperation. Theo, awaiting sentencing, expects Coral to walk away. She doesn't. POV Theo. Emotional beat: justice imperfect but real; love surviving exposure.

chapters.title: Letter #116
chapters.summary: Coral writes to Theo for the first time — a letter delivered by hand, across the hallway instead of the mail. Forgiveness offered not as absolution but as beginning. POV Coral. Emotional beat: tenderness after wreckage; roles reversed at last.

chapters.title: The Unscripted Concert
chapters.summary: Coral returns to the stage — not Vane's hall, but a benefit concert for the legal-aid nonprofit, playing a damaged, repaired cello. Theo sits in the front row. No reviews, no stakes, just music given freely. POV alternating. Emotional beat: second chances earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Next Door
chapters.summary: Epilogue months later: two apartments with the connecting door finally opened, letters framed on the wall, a new blank page waiting. Coral teaching, Theo rebuilding, both choosing each other daily. Final image: Coral writing letter #117 and sliding it under the door three feet away. POV both. Emotional beat: home found in a person, not a stage.
